claims.text: An ultrathin ALD-deposited interlayer on W particles will improve Cu wettability.
Improved Cu wettability from the ALD interlayer will reduce void formation.
The ALD interlayer will reduce phase separation in W–Cu composites.
Reduced void formation and phase separation will enhance thermal transport and mechanical durability.
Molten Cu will wet the coated W particles during spark-plasma sintering.
Spark-plasma sintering and mechanical alloying are existing powder-processing routes relevant to the proposed baseline.
Conventionally processed W–Cu composites typically exhibit interfacial voids and phase-separation defects.
The intervention is to apply an ultrathin wetting interlayer to W particles by ALD before sintering.
Sub-solidus vacuum sintering can promote rapid and uniform interfacial diffusion in the proposed coated W–Cu system.
The proposed sub-solidus processing will prevent high thermal gradients.
The ALD-originated coating will form a chemically compatible interface between W and Cu.
The ALD coating will reduce interfacial energy barriers between W and Cu.
Reduced interfacial energy barriers will enhance Cu wettability and interfacial diffusion on W.
Enhanced wettability and interfacial diffusion will produce a denser, mechanically robust W–Cu composite with higher thermal conductivity.
Relative to uncoated W–Cu composites, ALD-treated composites will have lower void fraction, better interfacial contact, and higher thermal conductivity.
Relative to uncoated W–Cu composites, ALD-treated composites will maintain or improve mechanical durability under high-temperature fusion-joint service conditions.
The intended service boundary is high-temperature heat-transfer service in fusion-reactor joint environments.
The optimal ALD interlayer material and thickness are not yet established.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis invokes improved wettability of molten Cu during SPS, while the stated processing boundary requires sub-solidus sintering without reaching melting temperatures. Under the stated boundary, Cu would not be molten, so the proposed molten-wetting mechanism is inconsistent with the processing conditions.
